newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines-Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines-Jan 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Hong Kong's future Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa plans to visit the United States and Europe to ease worries about Hong Kong's future.
-- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will meet 10 other Asia Pacific central banks in Shanghai in July to discuss cooperation among central banks in Asia.
-- MING PAO - Most legislative councillors think the Power and Priviledges Ordinance should be retained.

-- The head of China's Zhuhai city on the border with Macau, Liang Guangda, said Hong Kong investors would continue to enjoy privileges as foreign investors after Hong Kong's return to China. He said the project of the bridge to link Zhuhai and Hong Kong had already been submitted to Beijing for approval.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD - A potential exodus of top judges could leave the judiciary with a massive gap to plug by the time of Hong Kong's return to China on July 1.

-- A company controlled by the Guangzhou municipal government, Newman Overseas, plans to buy out Hong Kong-listed car maker Denway Investment, saying it will reduce the car company's stake in its lossmaking venture with Peugeot and boost its finances.

-- EXPRESS NEWS - The price of a taxi licence reached HK$3 million last weekend and taxi owners were considering raising rents by $50 per shift, which would make the lives of taxi renters more difficult.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Beijing-Kowloon and Shanghai-Kowloon through train would start to operate on January 1, and April 1.
-- SING TAO -- China's People's Liberation Army stepped up winter military training recently.
